message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long‑weekend holidays that Canadians can enjoy in 2023**.  
(“Long weekend” means the holiday falls on a Friday or Monday, or is observed on a Monday when it lands on a weekend, giving you a 3‑day break.)

| # | Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day (observed) | **Jan 2** | Mon | **Jan 1–3** (New Year’s Day on Sunday, observed Monday) |
| 2 | Family Day (Ontario, AB, BC, NB, PE) | **Feb 20** | Mon | **Feb 18–20** |
| 3 | Good Friday | **Apr 7** | Fri | **Apr 7–9** (Good Friday + weekend) |
| 4 | Victoria Day | **May 22** | Mon | **May 20–22** |
| 5 | Canada Day (observed) | **Jul 3** | Mon | **Jul 1–3** (Canada Day on Saturday, observed Monday) |
| 6 | Labour Day | **Sep 4** | Mon | **Sep 2–4** |
| 7 | Thanksgiving | **Oct 9** | Mon | **Oct 7–9** |
| 8 | Remembrance Day (observed) | **Nov 13** | Mon | **Nov 11–13** (Remembrance Day on Saturday, observed Monday) |
| 9 | Christmas Day | **Dec 25** | Mon | **Dec 23–25** |

> **Quick notes**  
> * Good Friday is a statutory holiday in all provinces except Quebec, so it gives a long weekend to most Canadians.  
> * Some provinces have additional holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in PEI, etc.). If you’re planning for a specific province, let me know and I can add those too.  

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app!
